operative_context: Availability state semantics must separate operational validity (whether an item exists and is managed) from temporary rental blocking (maintenance, manual restrictions, active rentals)
System must distinguish between different non-rentable states (deleted items, maintenance periods, manual restrictions, temporary unavailability) in availability semantics and query responses
Availability query API must clearly communicate the reason or category of unavailability to prevent user confusion about item recoverability
Item availability status must be tracked separately from item lifecycle state (creation, modification, deletion) to maintain semantic clarity
exceptions: Maintenance periods block rental activity and render items non-rentable, but may require distinct UI representation from other unavailability causes
Deleted items or operationally invalid records must not be surfaced through the same availability wording as temporarily blocked items
conflicts_or_obsolete: Current implementation conflates maintenance-related non-rentable status with other forms of temporary unavailability without semantic distinction (E5, E6)
Availability query results surface operationally invalid records using the same wording as temporarily blocked items, misleading users about recoverability (E5)
Implementation path uses existing non-rentable status handling for maintenance without confirming whether UI needs to distinguish maintenance from other temporary unavailability (E6)
notes: R50 targets the semantic separation of availability states to resolve ambiguity between operationally invalid items (deleted, non-existent) and temporarily unavailable items (maintenance, manual restrictions, active rentals). PRIMARY evidence (E5, E6) documents implementation conflicts where maintenance and other non-rentable conditions are conflated without semantic distinction. E4 raises the specific gap about deleted items lacking a clear lifecycle value. CONTEXT evidence (E13, E14, E15) provides neighboring availability management rules and identifies the related gap about deleted vs unavailable state ambiguity. The operative context focuses on the requirement to distinguish state categories in both internal representation and user-facing query responses.
